utilityName: City of Marble Falls Backflow Prevention and Cross Connection
testingFrequency: Annual for high health hazard devices
dueBasis: Marble Falls says high health hazard devices must be tested annually and that BPAT testers submit reports online through Envirotrax rather than paper reports to the City.
coveredPropertyTypes: Residential pools with auto-fill high hazard devices
coveredDeviceTypes: High health hazard backflow prevention devices
officialListLabel: Open Marble Falls registered backflow tester route
penalties: Marble Falls says BPAT testers can no longer submit paper test reports directly to the City; accepted reporting runs through the online Envirotrax system.
sourceExcerpt: Marble Falls moved BPAT report submission to VEPO Envirotrax, rejects the old paper-direct path, and requires annual testing for high health hazard devices.
verdictSummary: Marble Falls is a strong Central Texas VEPO page because it has a dated portal transition, high-health-hazard annual testing, paperless submission, and registered-tester workflow.
whoIsAffected: Marble Falls non-residential high-hazard sites, residential pools with auto-fill high-hazard devices, and testers submitting annual reports.
residentialNotes: Residential impact is strongest when a pool with auto-fill or another high hazard device creates a reportable assembly.
The City points annual questions to Development Services and the Envirotrax flow.
commercialNotes: Hospitals, restaurants, industries, and other non-residential high-hazard sites are the clearest annual testing cases.
BPAT report submission must follow the VEPO/Envirotrax process.

annualTesting.summary: Marble Falls requires annual testing for high health hazard devices and routes BPAT reports through Envirotrax.
highlights: High health hazard devices are annual.
The City names restaurants, hospitals, industries, and auto-fill pools.
BPAT testers use the online Envirotrax submission path.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the device is a high health hazard device.
Use the Marble Falls registered tester route.
Have the BPAT submit through Envirotrax.

irrigation.summary: Marble Falls does not flatten every residential device into annual testing; the stronger public trigger is high health hazard status, including auto-fill pool examples.
highlights: Auto-fill pools are named as a residential high-hazard example.
workflowSteps: Confirm whether the residential or irrigation-related device is high hazard.
Keep the Envirotrax report tied to the correct assembly.

fireLine.summary: Marble Falls centers its page on high health hazard devices and BPAT submission rather than a separate public fire-line rule.
highlights: Fire-line specifics should be verified with Development Services.
High-hazard classification is the public annual signal.
The VEPO/Envirotrax path still controls report submission.
workflowSteps: Ask Development Services whether the fire-related assembly is tracked as high hazard.
Submit through the Marble Falls Envirotrax route.
Use the Marble Falls page to determine whether annual high-hazard testing applies.
Use the registered tester route rather than a generic provider search.
Have the BPAT submit the test into Envirotrax.
Do not rely on direct paper submission to the City.
failureHighlights: The old paper-direct submission path is no longer accepted for BPAT reports.
High health hazard classification determines the strongest annual duty.
Registered tester status matters before treating a test as complete.

costBand.testingRange: Private Marble Falls quotes vary by device hazard level and property type.
costBand.repairRetestRange: Repair and retest ranges widen for high hazard commercial devices.
costBand.pricingNotes: The strongest cost-control point is using a BPAT who can complete the Envirotrax submission.
